subject: Compilation fails with "supernodal = TRUE" but not "supernodal = FALSE" on my device

messages.author: f5b13b580eb160db
messages.subject: Compilation fails with "supernodal = TRUE" but not "supernodal = FALSE" on my device
parts:
Hi! I am a fairly novice TMB user and currently I have rigged up a fairly complex mixed-effects model. I have consulted the CRAN documentation in search of potential ways to speed things up. Under the documentation for MakeADFun() it suggests that compiling with the "TMBad" framework rather than the "CppAD" framework, and setting supernodal = TRUE when calling compile(), can speed things up in some circumstances. I have been using the CppAD framework by default up to this point. When I tried to compile my function with framework = "TMBad" and supernodal = TRUE, it appears to fail. When I set supernodal = FALSE, and keep framework = "TMBad", it compiles fine. For reproducibility purposes, I was able to replicate this issue with the spatial.cpp file available on the Github documentation. Once again, works with supernodal = FALSE but not with supernodal = TRUE. The error messages are quite long and not super intuitive to my eyes; here is a screenshot of some of the messages in case you are interested:
I checked the documentation for TMB::compile() and it seems like setting supernodal = TRUE calls on a different library to do some of the sparse matrix calculations. I imagine the problem is that I don't have the proper version of this library installed, and I'm not exactly sure how to get it installed / how to check whether I have the proper version installed (I use R a lot but don't use C++ very much aside from TMB, and I think it is a C++ library that is being used).

I am running TMB 1.9.9 on R 4.3.2 with a Windows 11 x64 computer. Let me know if there's any additional information I could provide which may be helpful. 

Peter

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: Compilation fails with "supernodal = TRUE" but not "supernodal = FALSE" on my device
parts:
Peter,

Before spending time fighting with the compiler, it might be worth checking whether your model has the potential to benefit from these optimizations at all. As the documentation says, the optimizations targets sparse matrix factorization using alternative re-ordering methods. It is mainly intended for 3D/4D GMRFs (see for example 'ar1_4D' from the tmb_example folder).
The example you refer to (spatial.cpp) has a dense hessian matrix, and therefore won't benefit!
